chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: NTG white shows at Sebastian's, Ben Pollack and Harry James
summary: A brief experiment with white shows at Sebastian's nearly bankrupted him before it returned to black acts.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: At the end of the last reel, you were mentioning the
(Inaudible) bands that came into the Cotton Club.

Yes, I believe I mentioned the Cab Calloway Orchestra. I'm not sure, right off the top of my head, whether Ellington came in there or not. I know he came into the vicinity many times and played theaters and such. But I'm not sure whether he came in Sebastian's, but after that, the Les Height Band was also out of there, during the time that -- NTG was the initials of a production company around town that put shows on.

Or some -- I don't know what it was. I think it was NTG. They started to -- they gave Frank Sebastian a bill of goods and started white shows in Sebastian's Cotton Club for a short time. During that time, they brought a band from the East out by the name of Ben Pollack. During that time, Ben Pollack sent for a very good trumpet player by the name of Harry James, who joined him for his first big-time band and they worked there for quite a while and during those times, the Height band toured up and down the coast. So, that was the extent of our traveling through that particular band.
it was just a short time?
So the NTG operation wasn't a complete change of policy; (inaudible)?
For a while, they had -- it was for a

short time. They sold them a bill of goods, where they could feel as though they could bring something in, they brought some people in there that were a little out of context with the general type of entertainment that they had and it was very unsuccessful. As a matter of fact, it almost drove the man into bankruptcy.
So then they changed back to the black standard again and sort of pulled us up out of the -- sort of pulled him up by his own bootstraps, I guess.
